rules.sentence: A complete atrioventricular septal defect is the absence of ventricular and atrial septum segments.
This cardiac defect results in a sizeable left-to-right shunt—the shunt increases in the first week of life when the pulmonary resistance drops.[39]
There is a risk of heart failure when the pulmonary resistance drops after 2–8 weeks of life.
AVSD is frequently associated with Trisomy 21 and is initially treated with avoidance of excess oxygen and pharmacological treatment of heart failure.
The patient undergoes corrective surgery at 4-6 months, possibly earlier, if conservative treatment remains unsuccessful.
